facts.title: Octo Metric, LLC
facts.agency: Department of Homeland Security, U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS)
facts.procurement_type: Task order for IT support services under FAR subpart 8.4, issued as a total small business set-aside to GSA MAS 54151S holders
facts.est_value: Not stated; evaluated prices were $88,090,259 (AEX) and $100,598,462 (Octo)
facts.evaluation_scheme: Best-value tradeoff between price and non-price factors: code challenge (most important) and corporate experience
facts.background: On March 16, 2026, USCIS issued the RFQ under FAR subpart 8.4 as a total small business set-aside to holders of GSA MAS 54151S contracts. The solicitation contemplated a single fixed-price task order for IT services supporting USCIS's mission, including design, development, and maintenance of the current technological solution. Selection was a best-value tradeoff between price and two non-price factors, code challenge and corporate experience, with non-price factors described as significantly more important than price. The code challenge included a take-home portion and a live demonstration in which vendors implemented new requirements during a three-hour period, conducted via Microsoft Teams and recorded. Vendors were required to use Databricks, but the solicitation did not require Terraform. Six vendors submitted quotations on March 31, 2026. The agency rated AEX high confidence under code challenge and some confidence under corporate experience, with a price of $88,090,259, while rating Octo some confidence under code challenge and high confidence under corporate experience, with a price of $100,598,462. The agency issued the task order to AEX on June 22, 2026, and Octo, the incumbent, protested.

protester_grounds.claim: Octo contends the agency unreasonably faulted it for not deploying all new code challenge requirements to production, arguing that Terraform and Databricks software updates were beyond its control.
Octo contends the agency unreasonably found weak program management and methodology, asserting its personnel are highly trained and its response to the Databricks issue was nimble.

Octo contends the agency unreasonably found its solution lacked cost-effective platform methods based on high operational costs, arguing its required capabilities necessarily carry higher infrastructure costs.

facts.agency_position: The agency argues Octo conceded it did not deploy the new requirements to production, and that Octo chose to use Terraform and was responsible for tracking changes affecting it. It states the Databricks update affected all vendors, and that Octo spent over two hours resolving it. The agency also contends the team's interactions showed gaps in leadership and direction, and that Octo's design choices prioritized persistent operation without adequate cost controls.
facts.record_facts_protected: Octo's code challenge was rated some confidence, while AEX's was rated high confidence. The agency identified three aspects that decreased confidence in Octo's quotation: not all new code challenge requirements were deployed to production, weak program management and methodology, and high operational costs shown on Octo's cost tracking dashboard. During the live demonstration, Octo acknowledged it had not deployed anything to production and that it spent about two hours on a Databricks update within the three-hour window. Octo's corporate experience was rated high confidence. Octo's evaluated price was $100,598,462, compared with AEX's $88,090,259.
